name: IN-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: Incumbent Rudy Yakym running with large fundraising edge ($5.2M raised)
No polls or expert ratings; markets price Democratic win at ~4%
model.rationale: Northern Indiana's 2nd District leans heavily Republican, and incumbent Rudy Yakym holds a massive financial advantage over Democrat Jamee Decio, who has raised only about $356,000. Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 4% chance, and with no polls or expert ratings suggesting movement, the race stays firmly in Republican hands.
model.watch: A major fundraising surge or outside spending for Decio combined with a strong Democratic national environment could narrow the margin, though a Democratic win remains unlikely.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Indiana's 2nd District is solidly Republican territory, with a partisan lean of about 13 points toward the GOP. Incumbent Rudy Yakym, first elected in a 2022 special election, is running for reelection and has raised over $5.2 million, dwarfing the roughly $356,000 collected by Democrat Jamee Decio. A Libertarian candidate, William Henry, is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover this race, but prediction markets price Yakym's chances at about 97%. With the incumbent advantage, the district's lean, and the lopsided money race all pointing the same direction, Yakym is heavily favored to hold the seat in November.
